title: A hawk overfed will not come to the glove
summary: A young bird of the mews at Cnoc bheag, fed too heavy the evening before, will not answer Gormshuil nic Artair's call at the dawn rite; her father Artair, too stiff now to climb to the block himself, tells her plainly that a bird fed past its measure is as useless as one starved of it.

title: Gormshuil calls Mòd down alone for the first time
summary: With Artair's knees failed for the climb, Gormshuil nic Artair goes up to the mews block at Cnoc bheag before dawn and calls the shrine's hawk down with no one else to answer for the flight, three-and-thirty years old and, by her own later word, more frightened coming down than going up.

title: Death of Artair, hawk-keeper of Cnoc bheag
summary: Artair dies at Cnoc bheag in his own bed above the shrine, three-score and ten years old, and the keeping of the mews he had held the better part of his life passes without dispute to his daughter Gormshuil; the hill's households bury him facing the shrine rather than in any rite of the departed.

title: Gormshuil first names the vein An Seabhag Acrach
summary: Asked, as custom wants, to say a few words over her father's empty place on the bench, Gormshuil nic Artair tells the shrine's watchers for the first time that the vein under Muileann dhearg is itself a hawk of Mòd's kind, to be fed the measured handful and never glutted past it.

title: Hawk-keepers of the north coast come to hear her
summary: Word of Gormshuil's teaching, carried inland by a wool-buyer of Bàgh an t-Seabhaig, brings three keepers of the coastal shrines to Cnoc bheag to judge it for themselves; they stay a week among the coal-cutters' wives at the shrine's ledge and go home saying the teaching has lost nothing in the carrying.

title: Bàgh an t-Seabhaig elder questions Gormshuil's own hunger
summary: The eldest of the three coastal keepers asks Gormshuil, on the last morning of their visit, whether she has ever gone hungry enough herself to know the second half of what she teaches; Gormshuil answers that she has, twice, and disliked the lesson both times without forgetting either.

title: Gormshuil's first true congregation
summary: The watchers climbing to Cnoc bheag for the dawn rite grow past the number the shrine's ledge can easily hold, and Gormshuil, asked more mornings than not to give the teaching whole, gathers it at last into the shape it will keep for the rest of her life.

title: Taigh an t-Seabhaig raised
summary: Gormshuil's watchers, calling themselves a house rather than a congregation, raise a hall of timber and dry stone below the mews block at Cnoc bheag, giving the old dawn-hawk rite a roof of its own for the first time in its keeping.

title: A second house raised at Ros gheal
summary: Two of Gormshuil's pupils, a brother and sister of a coastal household, carry the dawn rite down to the shore at Ros gheal rather than make every fisher's family of that coast walk two days inland; Gormshuil goes down herself to judge the teaching had travelled whole.

title: A pupil reports the flood at Seann Vell
summary: A pupil of the Ros gheal house, present on other business when the river at Seann Vell breaks its banks and carries away the lower mills, calls the flood a kind of overfed hawk; Gormshuil tells him plainly that a river is a river and not a hawk, and sends him back to watch the mills rebuilt before he judges further.

title: Death of Gormshuil nic Artair
summary: Gormshuil dies at Cnoc bheag, two-and-sixty years old, in the season the house at Ros gheal marks its own eighth year, and is buried, at her own asking, on the open hillside beside her father rather than within the hall her own teaching raised.

title: Ùisdean mac Pàdraig marks the sayings he did not hear
summary: Gathering Gormshuil's teaching into a single book, Ùisdean mac Pàdraig travels as far as Ros gheal to set down what her pupils remember, marking plainly every saying he did not hear from her own mouth; when the book is finished the marked sayings far outnumber the rest.

title: Birth of Sìleas nic Fhearchair
summary: A daughter, Sìleas, is born at Cathair dhearg to King Fearchar Donn in the two-and-thirtieth year of his reign, when he is five-and-fifty years old; she is his only child to live.
